item.description:
An artifact can open in its own window, so you can read one or two while you browse the list, and the sidebar names the place you are in and lets you open a tag's collection from Go to… or from Info.
### What's new
- Open in New Window (⇧⌘↩, also in the Artifact menu and a row's context menu) shows the selected artifact's preview in a separate window, titled with the artifact's title, at the zoom the shelf had when it opened. The shelf keeps the keyboard and the selection; ⌘W closes the window, and moving the artifact to the Trash or deleting it closes it too. Asking again for an artifact that is already open brings its window forward. - The line under the wordmark names the place you are in, with its count: Shelf · 42 · 3 unread, Archive · 5, Trash · 2 · 248 KB. - A tag clicked in Info opens that tag's collection, an exact match, and the subheader reads Shelf › #design · 12. Choosing the place you are in leaves the collection; choosing another keeps it. - Go to Artifact… is now Go to… (⌘E). A query that starts with # lists the tags of the place you are in with their counts, most used first, and ↩ on one lands on its collection.
### Fixed
- With the sidebar hidden, ↩ in the description field now lands the keyboard in the page instead of stranding it.

The sidebar stays responsive on a large artifact, and the keyboard returns to the list after you edit a description.
### What's new
- The sediment command’s help is layered: sediment on its own prints a short overview, and each command and topic has a page of its own.
### Fixed
- Selecting a large artifact no longer freezes the sidebar. On a 10 MB artifact the list stalled for about a second at every landing, and again when the arrow keys passed over it. - After ↩ or ⎋ in the description field, the arrow keys move the selection again with no click in between.

Moving between artifacts gets easier: each one reopens where you left it, Back and Forward retrace your steps, and the shortcuts sit where Finder and Mail keep them.
### What's new
- Each artifact remembers where it was scrolled. Leave one and come back by any route and it opens on the passage you left, and it still does after a zoom change, a narrower window or a rewrite of its content. Closing the window or quitting forgets every spot. - Back (⌘[) and Forward (⌘]) in the View menu walk the artifacts you stopped on: one you stayed on for a second, or scrolled. Each lands on the passage you left, and an artifact moved to Trash since is shown in the Trash. - The Share menu reads Copy Link, Copy File, Share…. Copy File puts the artifact’s file on the clipboard, to paste into Finder, Mail or a message. Share… now sends the file instead of the link, so the person receiving it needs no Sediment to open it. - The sediment command reports each artifact’s link in its answers to add, update and find, so a script can open the artifact it just found. - Shortcuts follow Finder, Mail and Notes. In the Trash ⌘⌫ is Restore and Delete Now… is ⌥⌘⌫; in the Archive ⇧⌘A is Restore, so the shortcut that sent an artifact away brings it back. Rename File is ⇧⌘R, Toggle Sidebar ⌃⌘S, Open in Browser ⌘O, Go to Artifact ⌘E, Activity ⌥⌘0 and Reveal Shelf Folder ⌥⌘R. - The toolbar above an artifact ends in the ribbon from Sediment’s logo.
### Fixed
- With Info following the selection, the description is sized for the artifact it shows, and no longer keeps the last one’s height or scroll position.
